question: Why do low-frequency waves travel farther than high-frequency ones?
answer: Near the storm, both high-frequency and low-frequency waves are strong. High-frequency waves lose their energy quickly, so they fade close to the storm. The fast, low-frequency swell keeps going and arrives hundreds of miles away.
move: Far from a storm, only the long, low-frequency swell is left.
